summary: Orapa Airport serves the mining town of Orapa in central Botswana, home to one of the world's largest diamond mines operated by Debswana. The town itself is largely a company settlement built to support the Orapa diamond mine, which is why the airport handles primarily charter and corporate flights rather than scheduled commercial service. The facility is a small but vital link for the mining industry and the residents of this otherwise access-controlled community.
faqs:
Q: Are there scheduled commercial flights to Orapa Airport?
A: No, Orapa Airport does not offer regular scheduled passenger service. It primarily handles charter flights, private aviation, and corporate travel related to the diamond mining industry.

Q: Why is Orapa a closed town?
A: Orapa is considered a restricted settlement due to its proximity to the massive Orapa diamond mine. Visitors typically need permission or an invitation from Debswana or a resident before they can enter the town.

Q: How far is Orapa from Francistown?
A: Orapa is located roughly 240 kilometers west of Francistown in Botswana's Central District. The drive typically takes around three to four hours on regional roads.

Q: Does Orapa have an air traffic control tower?
A: As a small regional airport, Orapa operates with limited air traffic services. Pilots should consult current Botswana Civil Aviation Authority publications for operating procedures and frequencies.
transport_tips: Access to Orapa Airport is almost exclusively by pre-arranged vehicle, as there is no public transport serving the terminal. Most travelers arrange ground transport through their host company or accommodation in advance, since the town is access-controlled and outside taxis are not permitted inside. Self-drive visitors will need their own 4x4 vehicle suitable for the unpaved regional roads leading into the area.
local_tip: If you are visiting for business with Debswana, confirm your gate-entry clearance well before travel and carry your identification documents at all times, as security checkpoints around Orapa and the neighboring town of Letlhakane are strictly enforced.
